title: Reading Drill — Tracking damage to borrowed instruments — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Tracking damage to borrowed instruments — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The school music technician had been asked to investigate minor defects being discovered only before a lesson in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on reported damage per loan, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used inspection cards at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because the age of each instrument might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward checks at the return desk. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
